logline: In Gilead, a totalitarian theocracy built on the ruins of the United States, fertile women are forced into sexual servitude - and one Handmaid refuses to stop fighting her way back to the daughter taken from her.

renewal.note: Six-season run on Hulu concluded May 27, 2025. The series finale aired after the show was renewed and completed its planned story arc.

bollymeter.basis: Season 1 scored 94% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic of 92. IndieWire called it one of the best shows of the year. The premiere season won 8 Primetime Emmy Awards including Outstanding Drama Series.

pull_quotes.text: One of the best shows of the year so far, at times hard to watch but impossible to ignore.
This is probably the spring's best new show and certainly its most important.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 premiered April 2017 and became the first streaming series to win the Emmy for Outstanding Drama Series. Critics awarded it 94% on Rotten Tomatoes, with IndieWire calling it 'one of the best shows of the year, at times hard to watch but impossible to ignore.' The Hollywood Reporter named it 'the spring's best new show and certainly its most important.' Margaret Atwood's 1985 novel provided a blueprint, and creator Bruce Miller's adaptation was praised for finding new layers in the source material: Elisabeth Moss's performance as Offred was called one of the defining television performances of the decade. The 2017 political context sharpened every image of the red cloaks and white wings.

episode_reviews.title: Offred
episode_reviews.review_body: The Handmaid's Tale Season 1 Episode 1 'Offred' premiered April 26, 2017 on Hulu as the series premiere. Rotten Tomatoes holds Season 1 at 94 percent; Metacritic scored it 92. The season became the first streaming series to win the Emmy for Outstanding Drama Series, winning eight Emmy Awards total. IndieWire called it 'one of the best shows of the year, at times hard to watch but impossible to ignore.' The Hollywood Reporter named it 'the spring's best new show and certainly its most important.' The premiere establishes the rules of Gilead with visual economy and atmospheric dread rather than expository overload. Elisabeth Moss anchors the hour with internal narration that critiques the compliance it describes. The 'Blessed be the fruit' exchange in ordinary daylight is more chilling than any explicit violence the show deploys - the banality of the ritual the episode's most effective horror.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The series premiere establishes the rules of Gilead with visual economy and atmospheric dread rather than expository overload. Moss anchors the hour with internal narration that critiques the compliance it describes. The premiere’s willingness to be uncomfortable comes without exploitation.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first 'Blessed be the fruit' exchange in natural light - the banality of the ritual more chilling than any violence.

critic_note.text: At every corner, The Handmaid's Tale brims with invention.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 scored 90% on Rotten Tomatoes but critics noted the show moving beyond Atwood's novel into territory that felt both necessary and occasionally punishing. Audience scores began to pull away from critical scores.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 expanded beyond Atwood's novel and settled into a sustained bleakness, treating each new injury as something the narrative must earn. The 13-episode expansion gave the show room to explore Gilead's geography and the Colonies, and the world-building takes center stage. Response to the extended deferral of relief split, with some finding the pacing exhausting rather than purposeful.
seasons.season_over_season: Expands the world beyond the source novel with visual ambition; critics held but audience fatigue with perpetual suffering became audible.

bollymeter.basis: Season 3 scored 82% on Rotten Tomatoes - a meaningful decline from the first two seasons. Critics described a show that had settled into patterns rather than escalating, with Offred's story losing momentum despite individual strong episodes.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 dropped to 82% on Rotten Tomatoes as critics registered genuine concern about narrative stasis. June's ongoing resistance felt circular rather than progressive, and the 13-episode count stretched storylines that might have been sharper in fewer hours. The season finale, involving the children's escape from Gilead, gave critics and audiences a genuine release after several episodes of slow movement. The declining trajectory was acknowledged by trade press: IndieWire noted that the show was 'struggling to justify its existence beyond individual remarkable performances.'
seasons.season_over_season: The narrative treading-water problem becomes visible to critics; the season is saved by a strong finale but the show's momentum is clearly straining.

bollymeter.basis: Season 4 scored a series-low 69% on Rotten Tomatoes. Critics found the show struggling to generate dramatic purpose from June's story while the audience score divergence from critical scores widened substantially.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 registered the series' Rotten Tomatoes low at 69%, the clearest critical signal that the show had outlasted its narrative architecture. Critics acknowledged Moss's sustained commitment to the performance while questioning whether the writing gave June meaningful agency or simply relocated her suffering. The season introduced Canadian storylines that gave the world texture but not necessarily the momentum the critics were looking for. The audience score remained more forgiving than the critics, suggesting a loyal fanbase willing to follow the show's emotional logic even where the plotting failed.
seasons.season_over_season: The critical consensus turns: the show is praised for performance and production values while the narrative engine is questioned directly.

bollymeter.basis: Season 5 recovered to 80% on Rotten Tomatoes as critics welcomed narrative movement and a shift in June's role from passive victim to active agent. The Serena Joy arc was singled out as a genuine complication of the show's moral framework.

seasons.review_body: Season 5 recovers critical ground with an 80-percent Rotten Tomatoes score, as the uptick comes from a genuine shift in narrative purpose. The season's Serena Joy arc, which places June's chief tormentor in a position of vulnerability, adds moral complexity the show had been accused of abandoning. The Canadian setting gives the world a different texture, and the season interrogates its protagonist's choices rather than simply leaning on sympathy.
seasons.season_over_season: A genuine recovery - the Serena Joy inversion gives the show's moral stakes new life and critics take notice.

bollymeter.basis: Season 6 scored 87% on Rotten Tomatoes as the final season. Critics praised the closure it offered while the show's finale episode registered as IMDb's lowest-rated of the entire run, reflecting audience division over the ending.

seasons.review_body: Season 6 concluded a run that began as a cultural landmark and ended as a more contested piece of prestige television. Critics scored it 87%, approving of the finale year's sense of purpose and the emotional payoff for June and the show's core relationships. The finale episode itself became the lowest-rated of the entire run on IMDb - a divergence Screen Rant attributed to audience expectations for a more decisive resolution after six seasons. The show's 8 Emmy wins from Season 1 remain its defining legacy, and the final season's critical recovery suggests the series found a way to end with dignity.
seasons.season_over_season: Closes the arc with critical approval but a divided audience response - the finale's rating divergence tracks a show that ran longer than its optimal length.
